text:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — VegaCorp just hit a post-activation embedding surge, cost dashboard spiked 3.2x in the last 2 hours. Saw it on the alerts feed.
Omar Lee: Ugh. Do we have throttles on their route?
Casey Nguyen: Not yet, they’re on the default embed route. I can push a temporary rate cap. What SLA can we tolerate?
Maya Patel: @Casey please cap at 60req/min for embeddings for now. That should keep latency steady and slow burn.
Priya Shah: FYI Vega's CS contact mentioned they turned on a new batch job that embeds entire backlog. We asked them to pause but they want to avoid data loss.
Rui Zhao: If they're batching, recommend switching to our incremental KV caching first — that'll cut cost by deduping prefixes. Do we have a docs link to send them?
Casey Nguyen: Sending the quick guide in thread: https://redwood.ai/runbooks/cost-safeguard#incremental-caching
Maya Patel: Also flagged renewal risk if spend stays like this. Not urgent yet but we should prep QBR talking points around token-econ and ops safeguards.
Omar Lee: I'm running a 30d forecast with current rate and with the cap applied. Quick snapshot: current run rate ~ $18k/month -> with cap it'll be ~ $7k/month.
cost-bot: Alert created: ticket CS-4821 (VegaCorp embedding surge). Pager notified (#eng-runtime).
Priya Shah: Can we offer a short enablement session for their infra team tomorrow? 20 mins to walk caching + partial re-ingest patterns.
Casey Nguyen: I can do a quick call. I'll prep a minimal playbook and a sample CLI snippet to patch rate limits.
Maya Patel: Assign action items: 1) @Casey apply temporary rate cap (done when command exits successfully), 2) @Omar post forecast numbers to the ticket, 3) @Rui draft caching playbook link/email, 4) schedule 20m enablement with Vega.
Omar Lee: Forecast posted to CS-4821: `no-cap: $18,230/mo`, `cap-60rpm: $6,980/mo`, assumptions listed.
Rui Zhao: Drafted email & playbook bullets. Will attach a sample prompt sweep and KV cache config.
Priya Shah: Vega accepted 20m at 11:00 PT tomorrow. Please add the meeting invite and the enablement doc.
Maya Patel: For QBR prep — include a slide with: current vs. mitigated run rate, recommended guardrails (caps + caching), and renewal health flag at "watch". I'll add to the deck.
Casey Nguyen: Quick patch snippet to apply route cap (for engineers):
```bash
# set route capacity to 60 requests per minute
redwood routes update --customer vega --route embeddings --rate-limit 60
```
Maya Patel: Nice. Also suggest a temporary credits top-up offer: 2-week top-up with automated rollback when usage normalizes. Thoughts?
Omar Lee: Offer looks good — reduces churn risk. Add a clause: top-up auto-expire or convert to committed credits if they choose.
Priya Shah: Vega asked if we can automate a budget alert threshold for them (email + slack). Can we enable per-account alerts?
Casey Nguyen: Yep — enable alert on monthly projected spend > 120% of baseline. I'll add it to the ticket.
Maya Patel: Great. I'll capture all this in CS-4821 and include a short summary in the QBR prep doc. Closing loop: tagging #eng-runtime for any infra changes. :thumbsup: 
cost-bot: Action logged: rate-limit applied by Casey Nguyen at 3276543450.
Maya Patel: Thanks team — keep updates in the ticket. We'll review in the QBR readiness sync on Friday.
